title: Directions & Getting Lost
description: Asking the way and understanding the answer: left, right, straight on, near and far, and what to say when you're lost. People give directions by landmarks more than by street names.

phrases.english: Excuse me, could I ask you something?
phrases.registerNotes: The classic polite opener before asking the way. Numpang means to ride along or use someone else's space, so it's humble; Permisi, mau tanya (I'd like to ask) is plainer.
Swap in any place: hotel, pasar (market), halte bus (bus stop). The ya at the end keeps it soft.
phrases.pitfallNote: Put the place first and di mana last, the way people usually ask. Di mana is written as two words.

phrases.english: Is there an ATM near here?
phrases.registerNotes: Di dekat sini (near here) plus ada (is there) works for anything: apotek (a pharmacy), toilet, warung.
phrases.audioHint: Di dekat sini ada a te em?

phrases.registerNotes: Jauh? (Is it far?) on its own works too. Answers: dekat (close), lumayan jauh (quite far), sekitar lima menit (about five minutes).
phrases.cultureNote: Dekat often means close by motorbike, so asking whether you can walk gets a more useful answer.

phrases.english: Turn left at the traffic lights.
phrases.registerNotes: Lampu merah (red light) means the traffic lights, whatever colour they're showing. Belok kanan is turn right.

phrases.indonesian: Lurus saja, nanti di perempatan belok kanan.
phrases.english: Go straight on, then turn right at the crossroads.
phrases.registerNotes: Perempatan is a crossroads and pertigaan a T-junction. Nanti here means 'then, further along', and lurus terus means keep going straight.

phrases.english: On the left, near the mosque.
phrases.registerNotes: Di sebelah kanan is on the right, di seberang across the road, and di belakang behind.
phrases.cultureNote: Directions are usually given by landmarks such as a mosque, a minimarket or a petrol station (pom bensin), rather than by street names or distances.

phrases.registerNotes: Follow it with Bisa bantu saya? (Can you help me?)
phrases.pitfallNote: Hilang (lost, missing) is for things: paspor saya hilang. For yourself, say tersesat (having lost your way).

phrases.registerNotes: Literally 'this is where?', for when you're not sure where you are. Ini jalan apa? (What street is this?) gets you a name to give a driver.

phrases.english: Could you show me on the map?
phrases.registerNotes: Hand over your phone with the map open. Tolong makes it a little more polite: Bisa tolong tunjukkan di peta?
Toilet and kamar kecil (literally small room) are both polite; in someone's home, ask for the kamar mandi (bathroom). Signs say Pria (men) and Wanita (women).
phrases.cultureNote: Many toilets have a hose or a water scoop rather than paper, and public ones often charge a small fee, so carry tissues and coins or small notes.
